name: What Happens During an AI Visibility Website Audit

step.name: Step 1: Crawlability and Indexation Review — We’ll start by digging into whether AI crawlers can even access and understand your website’s pages. This means checking `robots.txt` files, `noindex` tags, and ensuring your XML sitemaps are correctly configured. We’re looking for any accidental blockages that might be preventing AI from finding your content. What's done looks like a clear picture of what AI can and can't see on your site.
step.text: Step 1: Crawlability and Indexation Review — We’ll start by digging into whether AI crawlers can even access and understand your website’s pages. This means checking `robots.txt` files, `noindex` tags, and ensuring your XML sitemaps are correctly configured. We’re looking for any accidental blockages that might be preventing AI from finding your content. What's done looks like a clear picture of what AI can and can't see on your site.

step.name: Step 2: Structured Data Inspection — Next, we'll confirm that any structured data (JSON-LD schema) on your pages accurately reflects the visible content. AI systems rely heavily on this data to categorize and understand your offerings. It’s crucial that what AI reads in the code matches what a human sees on the page. You’ll get clear insights into your current schema implementation.

step.name: Step 3: Content Quality and Clarity Assessment — We then evaluate your content itself, focusing on whether it directly answers user questions, its overall clarity, authorship, and sourcing. AI systems favor fact-dense, semantically relevant content. This step ensures your answers are concise and optimized for AI extraction. The result is actionable feedback on content improvements.

step.name: Step 4: Technical Control Evaluation — This involves reviewing server logs and search-platform reporting, like Google Search Console, to spot any issues with status codes, redirects, or rendering. We’re looking for anything that might impede how efficiently AI processes your site. You'll see which access controls affect different AI/search systems.

step.name: Step 5: Prioritized Remediation Plan — Finally, you'll receive a documented list of findings and a prioritized plan for fixing any identified issues. This isn't just a list of problems; it's a roadmap to improving your AI visibility. We aim to clearly separate confirmed technical issues from any predictions about AI visibility, giving you a clear path forward.
step.text: What to Do Next Once the audit is complete, focus on implementing the prioritized remediation steps. Remember, an audit is a starting point, and changes need time to be recrawled and reprocessed by AI systems.
